prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1194; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- Witnesses and the officer say the claimant was not in the vehicle when the crash happened.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The insured driver reported a low-speed head-on collision, and the claim was opened today. The claimant has retained counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: The driver is named on the policy, and coverage was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: The police report and scene photographs have been reviewed. The other driver, the witnesses, and the responding officer all describe the collision the same way. The officer and witnesses state that the claimant was not inside the vehicle when the crash happened.

Entry 4: The claimant has given the same account in every conversation so far, with counsel present. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and the damage visible in the photos lines up with the reported impact.

Entry 5: Medical records show neck and back strain, which fits the kind and force of this impact. No earlier injury to the same body areas is known. Treatment followed a typical course and tapered as the claimant improved.

Entry 6: Treatment has largely concluded and the claimant reports continued improvement. Next step is to request the attorney's demand package and finish the evaluation.
